title: Throwing a ball on the Moon: ballistic flight without drag
learningObjectives: Calculate the maximum height using ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g) from vertical speed and gravity
Describe drag-free flight as uniform horizontal motion x = U0 * t and vertical motion with V = V0 - g * t and y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2
Explain why a given throw rises higher when gravity is weaker

sources.title: Throwing a ball on the Moon (project-authored test text)
sources.attribution: Written by the Make knowledge interactive project team for testing.

explanations.text: In a vacuum there is no air drag, so weight is the only force after release and the trajectory is purely ballistic.

evidence.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all. Its flight is purely ballistic.

explanations.text: Horizontal speed stays constant while vertical speed decreases steadily under gravity, defining the time-dependent position.

evidence.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight and the ball moves x = U0 * t across the ground.
The vertical speed is V = V0 - g * t, and the height is y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2.

explanations.text: The top of the flight occurs when vertical speed reaches zero, giving ymax = V0^2/(2*g); weaker gravity yields proportionally greater height.

evidence.quote: The ball stops rising when V = 0, which happens at t = V0 / g.
Putting that time into the height equation gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).
